tasks.short: Use GIS analyses to investigate scientific questions

steps.what: Define the scientific problem, GIS method and exact analysis parameters
Execute the specified GIS analysis operations in the GIS application
Test sensitivity and check spatial analysis results against independent evidence
Interpret the scientific implications and explain limitations

tasks.design: Configure a native {OTHER} GIS processing model to replay the technician's selected analytical operations and record provenance. The technician still chooses the scientific method, tests sensitivity and interprets the result in {DOCS}; successful execution is not scientific validation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated analytical runs can require manually reconstructing an already chosen operation sequence.
tasks.enabler_now: Native processing models can reuse explicit inputs, methods and parameters.
tasks.still_hard: Spatial bias, uncertain source data and a method that does not answer the scientific question.
tasks.human_edge: The technician and scientist recognise what the evidence does and does not support.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat execution setup while scientific method and interpretation stay human.

reach.task: Explain spatial sensitivity of a result
reach.learn: Relate parameter choices to the research claim

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native GIS processing models can replay a fixed analytical sequence and preserve parameters; scientific suitability and interpretation remain separate judgements.

assumptions: Boundary is scientific analytical execution and interpretation, excluding maintained-database entry and generic project conversion. Allocate any shared operation once rather than adding its saving across tasks.

Technician produces dataset IDs and versions, coordinate system, spatial extent, method and operation versions, parameter values, null handling and output specification in s1's 30 hours. Data custodians produce the underlying datasets as existing work. Missing data or invalid schema stops execution for manual resolution in exception upkeep; no scientific-validity flag is assumed.
Test native GIS processing models first; s2's 30% represents observed repeated manual setup or orchestration, not calculation runtime or waiting.
Alternative parameter runs in s3 are chosen and assessed by the technician, with all existing sensitivity time retained.
unknowns: Stability of source schemas and methods
research_questions: Can a saved model reproduce a reviewed scientific analysis while retaining provenance and visible missing-data exceptions?

incremental.description: Processing-model maintenance and source or method exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70, gross=30 and net=22 after eight upkeep hours. Range assumes repeated manual orchestration for a chosen analysis; method selection and scientific interpretation retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify the user's GIS problem and collect relevant version and source evidence
Prepare a source-linked explanation and candidate support steps

loop.purpose: Draft a GIS support explanation from selected current guidance
loop.input: User question, environment version and technician-selected support extracts
loop.output: One draft explanation with source-linked steps and explicit unresolved questions
loop.check: Technician checks instructions against the actual GIS version, coordinate assumptions and stated problem, trying relevant steps on a safe copy before advising the user
loop.stop: One draft; missing source support, unsafe data changes or version ambiguity returns to manual diagnosis with no command execution
loop.why_not_simpler: Native knowledge lookup is preferred; unfamiliar free-text questions may need a short adapted explanation rather than a fixed response

steps.what: Provide technical assistance and guide the user through supported actions
Confirm the support outcome and record any remaining GIS issue

tasks.design: Use native {HELPDESK} knowledge lookup before drafting an adapted answer in {DOCS}. The technician verifies its meaning, assists the user and confirms the actual outcome; a model cannot close a ticket based on its own explanation.
tasks.previous_blocker: A known procedure can still require substantial rewriting for a specific GIS question.
tasks.enabler_now: Reviewed support-content drafting can supply a first explanation.
tasks.still_hard: A similar symptom may arise from different coordinate, data or application issues.
tasks.human_edge: The technician checks the user's context and observes whether the advice works.
tasks.altitude: Less initial explanation writing while live assistance and resolution decisions stay human.

reach.task: Recognise a GIS question requiring specialist help
reach.learn: Capture versions, data references and coordinate context

evidence.claim: TOPdesk summarises tickets and drafts knowledge items for review; this supports reviewed support-content preparation, not automatic GIS diagnosis.
Model knowledge: GIS support instructions must be checked against application versions and data assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is direct user support, excluding custom application development and separately owned data processing.

Technician captures question, application version, relevant dataset reference, coordinate context and selected guidance links in s1's 25 hours. User supplies the observed symptom and existing documentation owner supplies the source guidance. Missing context causes manual enquiry, not an inferred diagnosis or resolved flag.
Try native knowledge articles before a model; current lookup runtime earns no saving.
No credentials or unnecessary personal data enter drafting; destructive or production changes need a separate authorised change process.
research_questions: Does reviewed drafting reduce support preparation after counting corrections and unsuccessful suggestions?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=88, gross=12 and net=8 after four upkeep hours. Range assumes useful source-grounded drafts; live support, checks and user effort do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate GIS and positioning software options

steps.what: Research GIS or positioning-software capabilities and relevant evidence
Analyze representative data or prototypes to test system feasibility
Recommend systems design or support changes from the feasibility evidence

tasks.design: Keep exploratory research, feasibility analysis and systems recommendations with the technician using {OTHER} GIS or positioning tools and evidence in {DOCS}. Narrow coding, repeat processing and routine support opportunities are counted in their specific tasks rather than counted again here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exploratory feasibility questions may lack an agreed method or reliable baseline.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing tools support experiments, but do not establish a distinct repeated clerical saving in this broad duty.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether a prototype result generalises to real operating conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The technician can challenge an attractive capability claim using local evidence.

reach.learn: Translate geographic observations into system requirements

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: exploratory GIS or positioning-software evaluation requires selecting evidence and interpreting feasibility in context.

assumptions: Boundary is residual exploratory feasibility and design advice, excluding specific scientific analysis, user support and programming already described elsewhere. A local roll-up must allocate overlapping observed work once.

Technician selects research evidence in s1 and produces feasibility observations in s2's counted 40 hours before s3. Data custodian supplies representative source data as existing work; missing provenance or requirements causes manual clarification. No structured feasible flag is assumed.
Use native tools and existing documentation before custom automation; computation runtime is not new human effort saved.
Zero upkeep because this broad task receives no new tool or changed process.
research_questions: Can observed work be assigned to specific duties without double counting exploratory analysis?

already_counted.description: Research, feasibility analysis and design judgement

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. Specific processing or programming gains are not counted twice under this broad exploratory duty.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep current with GIS technology and professional practice

steps.what: Read current literature and assess GIS technology developments
Discuss developments with colleagues and participate in professional education or conferences

tasks.design: Protect critical reading and professional participation. Sources in {DOCS} can support learning, but a generated digest does not establish understanding or replace discussion with practitioners.
tasks.previous_blocker: Keeping current involves assessing claims against real geographic work.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology removes the need for professional learning.
tasks.still_hard: Separating a useful technical development from a claim with limited validation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician relates new ideas to source quality, spatial assumptions and operating constraints.
tasks.altitude: Learning and professional participation remain part of the week.

reach.learn: Explain applicability without repeating unsupported claims

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: critical professional reading and discussion require active understanding rather than only faster access to summaries.

assumptions: Boundary is learning and professional participation, excluding event booking and separately owned project research.
No structured learning-completed or method-valid flag is assumed; technician assesses sources and participates within the retained steps.
Use existing professional resources before new software; current search runtime is not labour saved.
Zero upkeep because no changed process or technology is proposed.
unknowns: Any separate repeated clerical burden around events
research_questions: Which professional learning activities lead to a method the technician can explain and apply correctly?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. Learning and participation retain their effort; no search or summary baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated scientific-analysis setup and first support drafts while retaining method choice, feasibility judgement and professional learning.
reach: Clarify software feasibility with system owners
skills_to_grow: Validate support instructions on safe data
role.ambitious_version: A GIS technician who can reproduce analytical work and explain its assumptions while giving reliable, context-aware support.

job.title: Geographic Information Systems Technologists and Technicians
